pull_request.title: Initial cli imp
pull_request.body:
This MR introduces the implementation of CLI for interaction with the teleport server.

## Build

In order to build the server and the application, one can run `make all`. This will produce two binaries in folder `./build`.

## Server usage

The server can be started by running `teleserver`.

```shell 
$ teleserver --addr :2022
``` 

## CLI Usage
Fields in `[]` are optional while fields with `()` are mandatory.

`[user]` values: (default `root`)
- `bob` 
- `root`
- `wrongsignedclient` 
- `no_common_name`
 
`[host]` listening server socket: default `localhost:2022`

### Start 

`start` spawns a new job in the server with a name equal to `(job_name)` and executable given by `(program args...)`.
The new job is owned by `[user]`.

```shell 
$ telectl -u [user] --host [localhost:2022] start --name (job_name) -- (program args...)

``` 

Example:

```shell 
$ telectl -u bob --host localhost:2022 start --name jobName -- $(which date) 
8d82833f-b138-41c5-bc58-05e164dfcb3a
```

### PS 

`ps` command returns the status of a job/jobs that were created in the server. 

If `[container_id]` is not provided it will list the full process list the `[user]` has access to, i.e. `root` has access to every job while other users only have access to their own jobs. If no jobs are available only the table header will be printed

If `[container_id]` is provided it will list only the process with `[container_id]` if the `[user]` has access. If the job does not exist or the user has no access to it an error message is printed.

```shell 
$ telectl -u [user] --host [localhost:2022] ps [container_id]
```

Example:

If no `container_id` was provided:

```
                   ID                  |   NAME   |   STATUS   | OWNER |      START TIME      |      EXIT TIME       | DETAILS  
---------------------------------------+----------+------------+-------+----------------------+----------------------+----------
  4fa2012e-aa9a-48e6-98d8-e663cf0960f0 | jobName  | Exited (0) | bob   | 2022-02-22T19:04:14Z | 2022-02-22T19:04:14Z |          
  d2d72788-fcc4-4c11-9832-623fb2860393 | jobName2 | Running    | bob   | 2022-02-22T19:04:21Z |                      |          
  b4305b8c-0dc9-4173-99f2-74e1d47c774a | jobName2 | Exited (0) | root  | 2022-02-22T19:04:28Z | 2022-02-22T19:04:29Z |      
```

If `container_id=d2d72788-fcc4-4c11-9832-623fb2860393` was provided:

```
                   ID                  |   NAME   |   STATUS   | OWNER |      START TIME      |      EXIT TIME       | DETAILS  
---------------------------------------+----------+------------+-------+----------------------+----------------------+----------
  d2d72788-fcc4-4c11-9832-623fb2860393 | jobName2 | Running    | bob   | 2022-02-22T19:04:21Z |                      |          
```

### Logs

`logs` creates a stream to output the execution of the program with id equal to `(container_id)`-
If the user has no access to `(container_id)` or it does not exist in the server an error message is printed.
If it runs successfully the output is printed to `stdout` and will block until the program execution finishes or a signal is sent to the client.

```shell 
$ telectl -u [user] --host [localhost:2022] logs (container_id)
```

Example:
```shell 
$ telectl -u bob logs d2d72788-fcc4-4c11-9832-623fb2860393 
Tue Feb 22 19:04:22 WET 2022
```

### Stop
`stop` command sends a signal to stop a process.
If the user has no access to `(container_id)` or it does not exist in the server an error message is printed.
If it runs successfully nothing is printed.

```shell 
$ telectl -u [user] --host [localhost:2022] stop (container_id)
```

Example:
```shell
$ telectl -u bob stop d2d72788-fcc4-4c11-9832-623fb2860393 

```

My point is that on the host machine, after some time, the kernel can reuse for any process, not necessarily processes related to the container lib, the same PID assigned to the job created by us.

Therefore, and if by chance we execute the Stop method for this UUID, we can send syscall kill to any other process on the machine whose PID is the same as the process we executed, even though our process has already died "years ago".

Therefore, the presence of this check to verify that the process is no longer running tends to prevent it from being possible to send signals to the PID if the job is no longer running. However, there is the possibility of the process ending between the check and the syscall KILL, but there is no major problem as the probability of the PID being reused is low as the process was terminated recently.

Nice point.

By default read changes the buffer and since we must return the bytes since the beginning of the program we will need to create a reader to keep the status for each subscription.

I made the changes to `buffer.Buffer` and now it is an `io.WriteCloser` and has a `Reader` method that creates a separate reader for each "subscription". This reader will wait until the buffer is closed, a new call to write, or if the `WakeEveryone` function is called.

pull_request.body:
This MR introduces the implementation of CLI for interaction with the teleport server.

## Build

In order to build the server and the application, one can run `make all`. This will produce two binaries in folder `./build`.

## Server usage

The server can be started by running `teleserver`.

```shell 
$ teleserver --addr :2022
``` 

## CLI Usage
Fields in `[]` are optional while fields with `()` are mandatory.

`[user]` values: (default `root`)
- `bob` 
- `root`
- `wrongsignedclient` 
- `no_common_name`
 
`[host]` listening server socket: default `localhost:2022`

### Start 

`start` spawns a new job in the server with a name equal to `(job_name)` and executable given by `(program args...)`.
The new job is owned by `[user]`.

```shell 
$ telectl -u [user] --host [localhost:2022] start --name (job_name) -- (program args...)

``` 

Example:

```shell 
$ telectl -u bob --host localhost:2022 start --name jobName -- $(which date) 
8d82833f-b138-41c5-bc58-05e164dfcb3a
```

### PS 

`ps` command returns the status of a job/jobs that were created in the server. 

If `[container_id]` is not provided it will list the full process list the `[user]` has access to, i.e. `root` has access to every job while other users only have access to their own jobs. If no jobs are available only the table header will be printed

If `[container_id]` is provided it will list only the process with `[container_id]` if the `[user]` has access. If the job does not exist or the user has no access to it an error message is printed.

```shell 
$ telectl -u [user] --host [localhost:2022] ps [container_id]
```

Example:

If no `container_id` was provided:

```
                   ID                  |   NAME   |   STATUS   | OWNER |      START TIME      |      EXIT TIME       | DETAILS  
---------------------------------------+----------+------------+-------+----------------------+----------------------+----------
  4fa2012e-aa9a-48e6-98d8-e663cf0960f0 | jobName  | Exited (0) | bob   | 2022-02-22T19:04:14Z | 2022-02-22T19:04:14Z |          
  d2d72788-fcc4-4c11-9832-623fb2860393 | jobName2 | Running    | bob   | 2022-02-22T19:04:21Z |                      |          
  b4305b8c-0dc9-4173-99f2-74e1d47c774a | jobName2 | Exited (0) | root  | 2022-02-22T19:04:28Z | 2022-02-22T19:04:29Z |      
```

If `container_id=d2d72788-fcc4-4c11-9832-623fb2860393` was provided:

```
                   ID                  |   NAME   |   STATUS   | OWNER |      START TIME      |      EXIT TIME       | DETAILS  
---------------------------------------+----------+------------+-------+----------------------+----------------------+----------
  d2d72788-fcc4-4c11-9832-623fb2860393 | jobName2 | Running    | bob   | 2022-02-22T19:04:21Z |                      |          
```

### Logs

`logs` creates a stream to output the execution of the program with id equal to `(container_id)`-
If the user has no access to `(container_id)` or it does not exist in the server an error message is printed.
If it runs successfully the output is printed to `stdout` and will block until the program execution finishes or a signal is sent to the client.

```shell 
$ telectl -u [user] --host [localhost:2022] logs (container_id)
```

Example:
```shell 
$ telectl -u bob logs d2d72788-fcc4-4c11-9832-623fb2860393 
Tue Feb 22 19:04:22 WET 2022
```

### Stop
`stop` command sends a signal to stop a process.
If the user has no access to `(container_id)` or it does not exist in the server an error message is printed.
If it runs successfully nothing is printed.

```shell 
$ telectl -u [user] --host [localhost:2022] stop (container_id)
```

Example:
```shell
$ telectl -u bob stop d2d72788-fcc4-4c11-9832-623fb2860393 

```

Wouldn't it make more sense to set this on the server's config than the client's?

I would also argue that as long as all of your chosen cipher suites are secure there is no need to set this. In go1.17 the field has been deprecated and has no effect https://go.dev/blog/tls-cipher-suites

pull_request.title: gRPC server implementation
pull_request.body:
This MR introduces the implementation of the gRPC server with the proposed API and the required certificates.

The API is located in `proto` folder and can be compiled with  `make proto`.

The certificates are located in `certs` folder and can be regenerated using  `make certs`. The script generates certificates for the `server`, user `bob`, admin `root`, and a user without common name `no_common_name`. Another certificate is also present `wrongsignedclient` which is a certificate that was signed with a different `ca`.

Server code is located at `pkg/server` and the bin executable can be obtained by `make all`.
